description: The whole system on one screen: components, the data that flows between them, and whether each one is alive right now.

panels.title: Saturation — where the time goes
panels.description: Each component's p95 latency as a percentage of a budget chosen for that hop, so components whose absolute latencies differ by orders of magnitude can be compared on one axis. The topology below shows what is flowing; this shows what is struggling. Budgets are in deploy/grafana/nodegraph.py.

panels.title: System topology and live data flow
panels.description: Every box is a component and every number on it is live. Liveness dots are green at 1 and red at 0. The scrape path is deliberately drawn: Prometheus has ONE target, and the frontend collects from Postgres, SeaweedFS, Valkey, Keycloak and the crawl_runs table on its behalf — which is also why a frontend outage blanks every other panel rather than showing them as zero.

text.fixed: Boxes are components; dots are liveness; lines are data flow. Every number is live from /metrics.

Traefik ingress
chat / keycloak / s3 / grafana .lab

Postgres 17 + pgvector
chunks · documents · users · runs

Crawler (batch)
discover → fetch → extract → chunk → embed

CronJob crawler-tick
every 5 min · reads crawl_control

External document cache
7 days, in SeaweedFS
collects Postgres · SeaweedFS · Valkey · Keycloak · crawl_runs at scrape time
Pause / Stop / interval are written to crawl_control by /admin and polled here
pod → node IP → Traefik → Keycloak (hairpin): the issuer string must match the browser's

panels.title: Component liveness
panels.description: 1 = the backend answered the last scrape. A collector at 0 with the frontend at 1 means one backend is unreachable and its panels are stale, not zero.
